questions.statement: Scan the notice. On which day and at what time does the library open on weekends?
questions.context: Lucia is practising scanning a short notice about Saturday library hours.

options.text: Saturday at ten o clock
options.feedback: Correct! Saturday at ten o clock is the exact opening detail stated in the notice, so it answers the scanning question precisely.

options.text: Friday at six o clock
options.feedback: The option Friday at six o clock is wrong because the notice assigns that time to a weekday closing detail, not to the Saturday opening.

options.text: Sunday at noon
options.feedback: The option Sunday at noon is wrong because the notice lists Sunday as a closed day, so it cannot supply the Saturday opening detail.

options.text: Monday at nine o clock
options.feedback: The option Monday at nine o clock is wrong because that detail belongs to the regular weekday schedule, not to the special Saturday timetable.

questions.explanation: Scanning means moving your eyes quickly to find one specific detail such as a time or date, without reading every word of the whole passage first.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Where does the announcement say students must meet at eight in the morning?
questions.context: Marco reads a school trip announcement to find the exact meeting place.

options.text: In front of the main entrance
options.feedback: The option in front of the main entrance is wrong because that place belongs to the afternoon return point, not to the morning meeting detail.

options.text: In front of the sports hall
options.feedback: Correct! In front of the sports hall is the stated morning meeting place, so it matches the explicit location detail in the announcement.

options.text: Inside the school cafeteria
options.feedback: The option inside the school cafeteria is wrong because the cafeteria is mentioned only as the lunch room, not as the meeting place detail.

options.text: Beside the bus station ticket office
options.feedback: The option beside the bus station ticket office is wrong because that office appears in a sentence about lost tickets, not about the meeting place.

questions.explanation: Detail questions ask for explicit facts stated in the text, such as places and names, and the correct answer repeats that fact using the same or similar words.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is a supporting detail from the paragraph, not the main idea?
questions.context: Sofia reads a paragraph about a school recycling project and its results.

options.text: The project teaches students to protect the environment
options.feedback: The option the project teaches students to protect the environment is wrong because that sentence expresses the whole main idea, not one concrete supporting detail.

options.text: Students collected four hundred plastic bottles in October
options.feedback: The option students collected four hundred plastic bottles in October is wrong in the opposite way because it is only background context about the month, not the measured result.

options.text: Students recycled two hundred kilos of paper in November
options.feedback: Correct! Students recycled two hundred kilos of paper in November states one measurable supporting detail that proves the project worked in that month.

options.text: Recycling is important for modern schools
options.feedback: The option recycling is important for modern schools is wrong because it is a general opinion that could fit any text, not a specific detail from this paragraph.

questions.explanation: A main idea states what the whole text is about, while a detail is one small proof or example, and tests often ask you to tell one supporting fact apart.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: According to the biography, in which year did she receive the national science prize?
questions.context: Diego reads a short biography of a Spanish scientist for homework.

options.feedback: The option in 2015 is wrong because that year marks when she finished university, not when she received the national science prize detail.
Correct! In 2019 is the year the biography gives for the national science prize, so it links the correct date detail to the correct award event.
The option in 2021 is wrong because that year refers to her move to a new laboratory, not to the prize ceremony detail.
The option in 2012 is wrong because that year describes her first scholarship, which is an earlier and different detail in her life story.

questions.explanation: Dates and numbers carry precise detail meaning in reading, so you must match each figure to the correct event instead of mixing two similar figures together.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which option gives the correct order of the main events in the story?
questions.context: Carmen practises ordering events after reading a story about a lost backpack.

options.text: She called the bus office, then retraced her steps, then found it
options.feedback: The option she called the bus office, then retraced her steps, then found it is wrong because that order reverses the middle steps given in the story.

options.text: She retraced her steps, then waited at home, then called the office
options.feedback: The option she retraced her steps, then waited at home, then called the office is wrong because waiting at home never appears as a story detail.

options.text: She found the backpack, then lost it, then called for help
options.feedback: The option she found the backpack, then lost it, then called for help is wrong because that chain places the finding detail before the losing detail.

options.text: She noticed the loss, then retraced her steps, then called the bus office and recovered it
options.feedback: Correct! She noticed the loss, then retraced her steps, then called the bus office and recovered it follows the exact sequence of details in the story.

questions.explanation: Sequence details answer when or in what order things happened, and time markers such as first, then, after that and finally show you the correct chain.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The text says: There is a five euro charge for the Saturday workshop, and places must be reserved. Which option restates this detail correctly?
questions.context: Pablo reads a text about urban bees for his English portfolio.

options.text: Visitors must pay five euros to enter the rooftop garden
options.feedback: The option visitors must pay five euros to enter the rooftop garden is wrong because the text says entry is free and only the workshop has a charge.

options.text: Workshops take place every day during the summer holidays
options.feedback: The option workshops take place every day during the summer holidays is wrong because the text limits the workshop detail to Saturdays, not to every day.

options.text: The Saturday workshop costs five euros and requires booking
options.feedback: Correct! The Saturday workshop costs five euros and requires booking restates the price detail accurately while paraphrasing charge as costs and reserve as booking.

options.text: The garden closes completely during the winter season
options.feedback: The option the garden closes completely during the winter season is wrong because the text only reduces winter hours and never states a full closure detail.

questions.explanation: Paraphrase means saying the same detail with different words, so a correct option keeps the facts identical while changing vocabulary such as fee to charge.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: According to the article, why do many teenagers feel tired in morning classes?
questions.context: Elena reads an article about teenage sleep habits and screen time.

options.text: Because schools now start lessons much later in the morning
options.feedback: The option because schools now start lessons much later in the morning is wrong because later start times are never given as a cause detail in this article.

options.text: Because late night screen use delays their sleep
options.feedback: Correct! Because late night screen use delays their sleep is the cause detail the researchers state to explain tired mornings among the teenagers studied.

options.text: Because teenagers need less sleep than small children
options.feedback: The option because teenagers need less sleep than small children is wrong because the article states the opposite scientific detail about sleep needs.

options.text: Because homework has completely disappeared from secondary schools
options.feedback: The option because homework has completely disappeared from secondary schools is wrong because homework load is never mentioned as a cause detail in the text.

questions.explanation: Cause detail questions ask why something happened in the text, and the answer is the reason the author gives, not a reason you invent from general knowledge.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What comparison detail does the review state about the two phones?
questions.context: Andres compares two smartphones in a product review for class.

options.text: Model A is heavier and more expensive than Model B
options.feedback: The option Model A is heavier and more expensive than Model B is wrong because it reverses both comparison details given in the review table.

options.text: Both models share exactly the same weight and price
options.feedback: The option both models share exactly the same weight and price is wrong because the review stresses a clear difference in both details.

options.text: Model B is lighter but has a shorter battery life than Model A
options.feedback: Correct! Model B is lighter but has a shorter battery life than Model A captures both comparison details exactly as the review table presents them.

options.text: Model A has a smaller screen but a better camera than Model B
options.feedback: The option Model A has a smaller screen but a better camera than Model B is wrong because screen and camera details are described as identical for both models.

questions.explanation: Comparison details use structures such as lighter than, the cheapest or twice as fast, and you must check which product each adjective really describes.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The report says: The local organisers cancelled the parade because they feared heavy rain. What does they refer to?
questions.context: Lucia reads a short news report about a town festival.

options.text: They refers to the visiting musicians
options.feedback: The option they refers to the visiting musicians is wrong because the musicians appear later in the sentence and cannot be the antecedent of that pronoun.

options.text: They refers to the food stalls in the square
options.feedback: The option they refers to the food stalls in the square is wrong because the stalls are objects managed by sellers, not the people who cancelled.

options.text: They refers to the festival posters on the walls
options.feedback: The option they refers to the festival posters on the walls is wrong because posters are things that cannot decide to cancel an event detail.

options.text: They refers to the local organisers
options.feedback: Correct! They refers to the local organisers captures the correct antecedent detail, since the organisers are the people who cancelled the parade because of rain.

questions.explanation: Pronoun references such as they, it or this point back to a specific noun detail, and finding the antecedent proves you followed the meaning across sentences.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Three statements match the text details. Which statement is NOT true according to the text?
questions.context: Jorge reads four short texts about transport and must spot the false summary.

options.text: The night bus runs every thirty minutes
options.feedback: The option the night bus runs every thirty minutes is wrong as an answer because that frequency detail is explicitly confirmed in the timetable paragraph.

options.text: Students receive a twenty percent discount with a card
options.feedback: The option students receive a twenty percent discount with a card is wrong as an answer because that discount detail appears clearly in the second paragraph.

options.text: The new cycle lane connects the station to the airport
options.feedback: Correct! The new cycle lane connects the station to the airport is the false detail, since the text says the lane connects the station to the university campus.

options.text: Tickets can be bought on the official mobile app
options.feedback: The option tickets can be bought on the official mobile app is wrong as an answer because that purchase detail is stated directly in the final paragraph.

questions.explanation: NOT true questions require checking every option against the text details, and the correct answer is the one detail that contradicts or never appears in the passage.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Why does the chef mention cooking beside her grandmother as a child?
questions.context: Ana reads an interview with a young chef about her restaurant.

options.text: To prove that her menu uses only local ingredients
options.feedback: The option to prove that her menu uses only local ingredients is wrong because local sourcing is never presented as an exclusive detail in the interview.

options.text: To show that cooking competitions are unfair to women
options.feedback: The option to show that cooking competitions are unfair to women is wrong because competition fairness is never discussed as a detail in her answers.

options.text: To complain about the high rent of city restaurants
options.feedback: The option to complain about the high rent of city restaurants is wrong because rent prices never appear among the interview details.

options.text: To illustrate how childhood memories shape her recipes
options.feedback: Correct! To illustrate how childhood memories shape her recipes explains why the detail about her grandmother kitchen appears, since it shows the origin of her cooking style.

questions.explanation: Authors include small details for a purpose such as giving proof, showing contrast or explaining a cause, and purpose questions ask you to name that function.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: According to the messages, which detail about the plan is correct?
questions.context: Raul reads a message exchange between two friends planning a hike.

options.text: Marta suggests bringing extra water for the group
options.feedback: The option Marta suggests bringing extra water for the group is wrong because the extra water detail comes from Diego message at the end.

options.text: Diego changes the meeting time from nine to eight thirty
options.feedback: Correct! Diego changes the meeting time from nine to eight thirty is the detail supported by his second message, where he moves the start earlier.

options.text: Marta cancels the hike because of bad weather
options.feedback: The option Marta cancels the hike because of bad weather is wrong because neither friend cancels and weather is never mentioned as a detail.

options.text: Diego offers to drive everyone to the trail
options.feedback: The option Diego offers to drive everyone to the trail is wrong because transport details never appear in any message of the exchange.

questions.explanation: Dialogue detail questions test whether you tracked who said what, so you must attach each plan change to the correct speaker and message.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which statement correctly describes a detail shown in the chart?
questions.context: Nora studies a bar chart about water use at home.

options.text: Cooking uses more water than laundry
options.feedback: The option cooking uses more water than laundry is wrong because the chart bars show laundry clearly higher than the cooking detail.

options.text: Garden watering is the smallest category of all
options.feedback: The option garden watering is the smallest category of all is wrong because the smallest bar detail belongs to cleaning, not to garden watering.

options.text: Showering accounts for the largest share at forty percent
options.feedback: Correct! Showering accounts for the largest share at forty percent matches the tallest bar detail and the percentage label shown in the chart.

options.text: Laundry and cleaning together reach seventy percent
options.feedback: The option laundry and cleaning together reach seventy percent is wrong because their combined bars total only thirty five percent in the chart detail.

questions.explanation: Visual details in charts must be read exactly, checking labels and units, because a small shift in numbers or categories changes the factual answer completely.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: A classmate wrote: Dolphins fall into a deep full sleep every night. Which option corrects the false detail?
questions.context: Iker reads a passage about dolphins for a science and English task.

options.text: Dolphins sleep with half their brain awake while floating near the surface
options.feedback: The option dolphins sleep with half their brain awake while floating near the surface is wrong as a correction because it adds an unverified floating detail.

options.text: Dolphins rest one brain half at a time while continuing to swim slowly
options.feedback: Correct! Dolphins rest one brain half at a time while continuing to swim slowly fixes the false detail by replacing full sleep with the half brain rest described.

options.text: Dolphins never sleep because they must breathe consciously
options.feedback: The option dolphins never sleep because they must breathe consciously is wrong because the passage explicitly rejects that never sleep detail as a myth.

options.text: Dolphins sleep eight hours on the sea floor
options.feedback: The option dolphins sleep eight hours on the sea floor is wrong because the sea floor detail contradicts the swimming and breathing facts in the passage.

questions.explanation: Correcting a false statement means keeping its topic but fixing the wrong detail, so the right option changes only the inaccurate number, name or place.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Original detail: The town council provided funds, and then volunteers planted fifty trees. Which paraphrase keeps all details accurate?
questions.context: Sara must choose the sentence that best paraphrases a detail.

options.text: The volunteers planted the trees after the funds arrived from nowhere
options.feedback: The option the volunteers planted the trees after the funds arrived is wrong because it reverses the cause detail and makes funding the later event.

options.text: The town council donated the funds and the tools together
options.feedback: The option the town council donated the funds and the tools together is wrong because the council detail covers only funds, not tools.

options.text: The schoolchildren collected the funds for new trees
options.feedback: The option the schoolchildren collected the funds for new trees is wrong because it changes the agent detail from council to schoolchildren.

options.text: After receiving council funds, the volunteers planted fifty trees
options.feedback: Correct! After receiving council funds, the volunteers planted fifty trees preserves the agent, quantity and sequence details while restructuring the original sentence.

questions.explanation: A good paraphrase of a detail keeps every fact the same, including agents and quantities, while swapping sentence structure and synonyms for key terms.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The label says: Clean the wound, apply a thin layer once daily, then cover. Which option follows every detail?
questions.context: Tomas reads instructions for a first aid kit in the school lab.

options.text: Apply the gel twice daily after cleaning the wound
options.feedback: The option apply the gel twice daily after cleaning the wound is wrong because the label restricts use to once daily, not twice daily.

options.text: Clean the wound, apply a thin layer once daily and cover it
options.feedback: Correct! Clean the wound, apply a thin layer once daily and cover it reproduces all three instruction details of cleaning, quantity and frequency accurately.

options.text: Mix the gel with hot water before application
options.feedback: The option mix the gel with hot water before application is wrong because mixing introduces a step detail that never appears in the instructions.

options.text: Use the gel only when the wound bleeds heavily
options.feedback: The option use the gel only when the wound bleeds heavily is wrong because that condition detail limits use in a way the label never states.

questions.explanation: Instructional details tell you the exact steps, quantities and warnings, and one missed word such as before or only can make an answer dangerously wrong.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which detail do both film reviews share?
questions.context: Alba reads two short reviews of the same film for a comparison task.

options.text: Both reviewers praise the musical soundtrack highly
options.feedback: The option both reviewers praise the musical soundtrack highly is wrong because only the second review mentions music as a positive detail.

options.text: Both reviewers criticise the slow opening twenty minutes
options.feedback: The option both reviewers criticise the slow opening twenty minutes is wrong because only the first review complains about that pacing detail.

options.text: Both reviewers agree the ending felt rushed and unclear
options.feedback: The option both reviewers agree the ending felt rushed and unclear is wrong because the second reviewer calls the ending the strongest part.

options.text: Both reviewers note the lead actor gives a strong performance
options.feedback: Correct! Both reviewers note the lead actor gives a strong performance is the one detail repeated in both texts, even though their overall verdicts differ.

questions.explanation: When two texts describe the same topic, the shared detail is the fact both mention, while differences show each writer selected separate supporting evidence.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which summary includes all the key factual details of the original text?
questions.context: Mario evaluates two summaries of a text about solar schools.

options.text: Panels were installed in twelve rural schools in Andalusia last spring
options.feedback: The option panels were installed in twelve rural schools in Andalusia last spring is wrong for completeness because it omits the savings result detail entirely.

options.text: Electricity bills fell by thirty percent after installation
options.feedback: The option electricity bills fell by thirty percent after installation is wrong for completeness because it omits the who and where details of the schools.

options.text: Solar panels produce clean energy for many buildings
options.feedback: The option solar panels produce clean energy for many buildings is wrong for completeness because it is too general and drops every specific detail.

options.text: Twelve rural schools in Andalusia installed panels last spring and cut bills by thirty percent
options.feedback: Correct! Twelve rural schools in Andalusia installed panels last spring and cut bills by thirty percent includes the who, where, when and result details together.

questions.explanation: A complete summary must include all key details such as who, what, where and result, and an option missing one of those pillars is incomplete.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Question: Which weekday train departs from platform four at seven fifteen? Which option answers it with correct details?
questions.context: Julia analyses a tricky exam question about a train timetable.

options.text: The seven forty five train arrives at eight thirty
options.feedback: The option the seven forty five train arrives at eight thirty is wrong as the question asks, because that detail answers arrival, not the required departure platform.

options.text: The eight fifteen train leaves from platform two
options.feedback: The option the eight fifteen train leaves from platform two is wrong because that platform detail belongs to the Sunday service, not to the weekday timetable asked.

options.text: The seven thirty train is cancelled on Fridays
options.feedback: The option the seven thirty train is cancelled on Fridays is wrong because cancellation is a footnote detail for holidays, not for regular Fridays.

options.text: The seven fifteen train departs from platform four on weekdays
options.feedback: Correct! The seven fifteen train departs from platform four on weekdays is the only option whose train time, platform and weekday condition all match the timetable details.

questions.explanation: Good detail questions have one answer supported by a stated line, whiledistractor options refer to nearby lines that look similar but answer a different question.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which strategy best helps a student answer reading detail questions accurately and quickly?
questions.context: Hugo reviews his own strategy for detail questions before the final test.

options.text: Read the whole passage slowly and memorise every sentence
options.feedback: The option read the whole passage slowly and memorise every sentence is wrong because memorising everything wastes time and ignores targeted scanning as a detail strategy.

options.text: Choose the option with the most difficult vocabulary words
options.feedback: The option choose the option with the most difficult vocabulary words is wrong because word difficulty never signals which detail correctly answers the question stem.

options.text: Always select the longest option as the correct detail
options.feedback: The option always select the longest option as the correct detail is wrong because length is a test design accident, not evidence that the details match the passage.

options.text: Read the stem first, underline detail anchors, then scan for them
options.feedback: Correct! Read the stem first, underline detail anchors, then scan for them describes the efficient strategy because it directs attention to names, dates and numbers before answering.

questions.explanation: Expert readers first read the question stem, underline key detail words such as names and figures, then scan the passage for those anchors before choosing an answer.
questions.subject: ingles
